- key_parameters: mode="onDisk"=Enables the memory-efficient on-disk data storage model in readMSData, which is faster for object creation and supports multiple MS levels ;; msLevel=Integer specifying the MS level of spectra to import in readMSData ;; copy=TRUE=Copies general metadata (instrument info, processing descriptions) from the originating file when exporting with writeMSData ;; t=Numeric threshold in removePeaks below which peak intensities are set to 0 ;; mzlim=Numeric vector of length 2 specifying the m/z range to retain in filterMz/trimMz ;; method=Character string specifying the quantification method (e.g., "trap", "max", "sum" for isobaric tags; "count", "SIn" for label-free) ;; reporters=A ReporterIons object defining the expected m/z and width of reporter peaks ;; strict=Logical defining whether data points outside the reporter m/z width are considered in quantify ;; pNA=Percentage of accepted missing values per feature in filterNA ;; groupBy=A factor defining how to aggregate features (e.g., spectra to proteins) in combineFeatures
- alternatives: mode="inMemory" vs mode="onDisk" in readMSData (onDisk is highly preferred for large datasets to save RAM, though on-the-fly spectrum access is slightly slower) ;; openIDfile (from mzR) vs mzID (from mzID) for parsing identification data (MSnbase uses the faster openIDfile internally via readMzIdData) ;; ExpressionSet (from Biobase) vs MSnSet (MSnbase's proteomics-specific extension; objects can be coerced between these classes using as(object, "ExpressionSet") or as(object, "MSnSet"))
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing raw mass spectrometry proteomics data, specifically for importing XML-based formats (mzML, mzXML, mzData) or peak lists (mgf), performing spectrum-level manipulations (cleaning, smoothing, peak picking), and quantifying features using isobaric tags (iTRAQ, TMT) or label-free methods.
- pitfalls: On-disk OnDiskMSnExp objects cannot be directly saved and loaded using save() and load() (workaround: coerce to in-memory first using as(object, "MSnExp")) ;; removePeaks does not delete peaks from the spectrum; it only sets their intensities to 0 (you must call clean() afterward to physically remove them and reduce object size) ;; In socket-based parallel processing, connections can get stuck (workaround: disable parallel processing with register(SerialParam()) or explicitly initialize the parallel setup using doParallel at the start of the script) ;; When combining different MSnSet experiments along columns, you must update sample names and feature variable labels first (using updateSampleNames and updateFvarLabels) to avoid conflicts and overwriting of metadata.

workflows.name: isobaric_tagging_quantitation
workflows.intent: Import raw MS data, integrate peptide identifications, clean spectra, quantify reporter ions, correct for isotopic impurities, normalize, and aggregate spectrum-level data to protein-level abundances.
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw MS data ;; 2. Integrate peptide identification data ;; 3. Filter out unidentified spectra ;; 4. Clean low-intensity peaks and remove empty data points ;; 5. Focus on the reporter ion m/z range ;; 6. Quantify reporter ions ;; 7. Filter out features with missing values ;; 8. Correct for isotopic impurities ;; 9. Normalize reporter intensities ;; 10. Aggregate spectrum-level quantitation to protein-level abundances
workflows.code:
msexp <- readMSData(quantFile, verbose = FALSE)
msexp <- addIdentificationData(msexp, id = identFile)
msexp <- removeNoId(msexp)
experiment <- removePeaks(msexp, t = 400, verbose = FALSE)
experiment <- clean(experiment, verbose = FALSE)
experiment <- filterMz(experiment, mzlim = c(112,120))
qnt <- quantify(experiment, method = "trap", reporters = iTRAQ4, strict = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
qnt <- filterNA(qnt, pNA = 0)
qnt.crct <- purityCorrect(qnt, impurities)
qnt.max <- normalise(qnt, "max")
gb <- fData(qnt)$ProteinAccession
qnt2 <- combineFeatures(qnt, groupBy = gb, method = "median")

workflows.name: label_free_quantitation
workflows.intent: Perform label-free MS2 quantitation using spectral counting or spectral index (SIn) methods.
workflows.stages: 1. Import raw MS data ;; 2. Integrate peptide identification data ;; 3. Filter out unidentified spectra ;; 4. Quantify using spectral counting or SIn method ;; 5. Aggregate features to protein level
workflows.code:
msexp <- readMSData(quantFile, verbose = FALSE)
msexp <- addIdentificationData(msexp, id = identFile)
msexp <- removeNoId(msexp)
sc <- quantify(msexp, method = "count")
sc <- combineFeatures(sc, groupBy = fData(sc)$DatabaseAccess, method = "sum")
siquant <- quantify(msexp, method = "SIn")
